facts.quote: There is an available PASSPORT slot that does not exceed the CMS-authorized limit for individuals enrolled for the waiver program year.
facts.title: Rule 5160-31-03 | PASSPORT HCBS waiver program: eligibility and enrollment.

facts.claim: Secondary sources put the PASSPORT cap at about 39,807 beneficiaries per year, which does not match the ~33,000 simultaneous figure cited elsewhere.
facts.quote: This waiver is approved for a maximum of approximately 39,807 beneficiaries per year.
facts.title: Ohio Medicaid PASSPORT Waiver: Benefits & Eligibility

facts.claim: A secondary source says PASSPORT has historically not had a chronic statewide waitlist, with only brief local waits when the enrollment ceiling fills; current status must be confirmed with the AAA.
facts.quote: PASSPORT has historically operated without a chronic statewide waitlist when CMS-approved enrollment ceiling has room.
facts.title: Ohio PASSPORT Waiver 2026: Eligibility, Services & Apply

facts.claim: A secondary source reports multi-year waitlists in many counties for the DODD Individual Options waiver.
facts.quote: DODD waivers, particularly the Individual Options Waiver, have historically had multi-year waitlists in many counties
facts.title: Ohio Medicaid HCBS Waivers 2026: PASSPORT, AL, OHCW & More

facts.claim: Ohio had about 2.27 million residents aged 65 and older in 2024, per USAFacts (compiled from Census data).
facts.quote: About 2.27 million Ohio residents were aged 65 and older in 2024.
facts.title: How many people live in Ohio?

facts.claim: The 65+ share of Ohio's population was 19.1% in 2024, versus 18% nationally, per USAFacts.
facts.quote: That represents 19.1% of the state’s population compared with 18% in the US overall.
facts.title: How many people live in Ohio?

facts.claim: Ohio's senior population grew by more than 10% between 2020 and 2024, according to Census Vintage 2024 estimates reported by the Dayton Daily News.
facts.quote: The state’s senior population increased by more than 10% between 2020 and 2024
facts.title: Older adults outnumber children in more than 1 in 4 Ohio counties

facts.claim: Scripps Gerontology Center researchers project that by 2025 more than a quarter of Ohioans will be 60 or older.
facts.quote: by 2025, more than 1 in 4 Ohioans will be age 60 and older.
facts.title: Ohio Population Research

facts.claim: Nonmedical home health and personal care agencies have needed an ODH license since July 1, 2022 (search excerpt; page not fetched).

facts.quote: a non-refundable application fee of $250.00.
